source.title: Comparison of Optimizers for Fault Isolation and Diagnostics of Control Rod Drives

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper; no apparent cutoff or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizers on held-out performance in simulated control-rod-drive fault classification, a new application setting for the optimizer-generalization claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out classification results for its optimizers. Its optimizer rankings based on validation loss and convergence are not rows for the claim because they do not measure the training–test gap.
record.test_reason: The study compares adaptive optimizers with SGD using held-out fault-classification accuracy in a new setting. This bears on V4; measuring a training–test gap is not required to compare held-out performance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the optimizer conclusion: under the tested dataset, methods, and selection criteria, Nadam was preferred for most tasks, and the authors recommend treating the number of assessment runs as a hyperparameter. They also conclude that current monitoring supports fault isolation and diagnosis, while acknowledging that real-world validation remains necessary.
record.recipe_differences: Default Keras optimizers were compared on simulated FMCRD fault isolation and diagnosis using 1D-CNN models, rather than the claim’s image and language benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: The preferred optimizer varied with task, monitored property, and number of runs; test classification accuracy was reported as equal across optimizers.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Prognostics and Health Management
record.problems: Simulated data rather than real-world experimental data; the paper says real-world robustness needs validation. Test accuracy is reported in aggregate across optimizers, without separate values or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Validation-loss rankings and convergence-rate comparisons in Sections IV-A, IV-B, and IV-C were not extracted because they do not measure held-out performance or the training–test gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.

Image and language benchmarks; learning-rate and decay-schedule tuning; momentum SGD; equal training performance; broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers. The study uses default Keras optimizer hyperparameters.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations to large-batch training.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly says validation loss does not measure held-out performance: validation loss is a held-out measure and its optimizer comparisons can bear on V4. Those comparisons are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing. Convergence speed alone does not establish a generalization advantage. The equal test accuracies do not warrant the record's blanket challenges verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models.
Image-classification and language benchmarks; comparison with momentum SGD; training performance versus the training–test gap; broader tuning, weight decay, and switching optimizers.
Batch-size effects and adaptations to large-batch training.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures of the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: encoder-decoder structured 1D-CNN classifier
rows.operation_detail: Compared test classification accuracy across the four optimizers.
rows.value: All optimizers produced the same test result; the test confusion matrix shows 100% identification of all faults with SGD.
rows.note: Aggregate statement across optimizers; the text does not give separate accuracy values for each optimizer.
rows.check: Specify SGD as the comparator: all four optimizers achieved 100% test accuracy with current monitoring. This is a reported test result, not an accuracy distribution across assessment runs.

rows.subject: encoder-decoder structured 1D-CNN classifier
rows.operation_detail: Compared test classification accuracy across the four optimizers.
rows.note: Aggregate statement across optimizers; the text does not give separate accuracy values for each optimizer.
rows.check: Specify SGD as the comparator and retain the best-model selection condition: all four optimizers achieved 100% test accuracy when testing their best models. This does not establish equal performance across runs; the authors report less reliable validation performance for Adam.

relationships.condition: Simulated FMCRD fault classification with current monitoring and default Keras optimizers
relationships.reason: R1 reports 100% test accuracy for SGD and all adaptive optimizers, identifying a setting without an adaptive-optimizer disadvantage; this qualifies rather than refutes an 'often' claim.
relationships.display_finding: SGD and adaptive optimizers reportedly achieved perfect test accuracy, but this result remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Simulated FMCRD fault classification with torque monitoring, testing the best models
relationships.reason: R2 reports 100% test accuracy for all optimizers after best-model selection; equality under this selection does not establish equal typical performance across runs.
relationships.display_finding: Selected best models reportedly achieved perfect test accuracy across optimizers, but the result remains unverified and does not establish equal typical performance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Fault classification using current or torque in the simulated FMCRD system
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports identical test results across optimizers for current and 100% test accuracy for all optimizers with torque, rather than an adaptive-optimizer test-performance disadvantage (R1, R2). These results do not measure a training–test gap.
